key_reasons.reason: A collective 40-class quantum decision is not, by itself, the missing computational role. Writing p_r(x)=Tr[E_r(x)ρ(x)], with E_r≥0 and Σ_r E_r=I, establishes a normalized decision rule, but leaves the substantive word-to-evidence computation unspecified. Frame normalization or state discrimination alone repeats the PGM/POVM territory; supplying ρ through previously described memory, contextual-overlap, tensor, or word-index transport paths does not establish a new task computation.

An instrument-based replacement g_rt=Tr[E_r I_t(ρ)], followed by α_rt=g_rt/Σ_j g_rj and z_r=w_rᵀΣ_t α_rt v_t+b_r, still performs class-conditioned marginal token weighting. Changing the instrument, calling its outcomes values, or coupling its parameters to the decision is insufficient to distinguish it from the audited score, backaction, joint-value and history-posterior constructions.

key_reasons.reason: Joint witness selection could change the task computation—for example, z_r=Σ_ij π_rij F_r(v_i,v_j)—but that expression is only a classical task architecture until a specific quantum operation, indispensable interference term and ancestry-distinguishing prediction are derived. Generic pair overlap, determinant/Gram scoring, entanglement, or coherent index propagation does not supply that distinction. I have not derived a surviving mechanism.
